Ordnance 0.4.4. The game boots from Ordnance's own loader, and F10 opens mod options and keybinds in a mission.

## What's new

**One boot, and it is Ordnance.** Deploy writes the file swaps and starts addons from a single boot script. You do not install Chef, Rat's Shared Loader, or Boot Mod Loader.

**F10 opens mod options in game.** The menu follows the resolution you are playing at. Arrow keys move one row at a time. Right arrow rebinds a key. Enter stays the chat key. Mods that register options or keybinds through the Chef, Boot Mod Loader, or Mod Options menus show up here. Opening the menu no longer freezes the frame, and quitting after you have opened it no longer hangs.

**Share a profile as a list.** Export writes the mod order, what is enabled, and the option choices. It does not include the mod files. Import turns those boxes on for mods you already have and lists the ones you are missing by name.

**A bad mod no longer fails the whole deploy.** Stat plans apply onto the tables the game has now. One mod that cannot be applied is left out, and the rest still deploy.

**Browser extension 1.0.4.** On a Nexus Files tab, the button next to Manual download is Ordnance. It used to stay "Mod manager download" while the button at the top of the page was already ours.

Sign in to Nexus Mods still says Coming soon. An API key in Settings is how update checks reach Nexus until Nexus issues a client id.

## What Ordnance does

**Import from your current mod manager.** One-click import from HD2 Arsenal and Echelon — plus the older HD2 mod manager, Vortex, and your Downloads folder, with names, on/off state, and options intact.

**Automatic update checking and (optionally) downloading.** Ordnance checks every mod against its source — AyakaMods, GitHub, GameBanana, ModWorkshop, and Nexus Mods — and, when you enable it, downloads and installs the ones it can fetch itself.

**One deploy, everything enabled.** Merge mods and generated stat-plan edits into a single sealed swap and a single boot script. No per-mod loader conflicts.

## Get it

| Platform | Download |
| --- | --- |
| Windows | `Ordnance-0.4.4-windows-x64-setup.exe` |
| Windows: no install | `Ordnance-0.4.4-windows-x64-portable.zip` |
| Linux (Debian/Ubuntu) | `Ordnance-0.4.4-linux-amd64.deb` |
| Linux (Fedora/openSUSE) | `Ordnance-0.4.4-linux-x86_64.rpm` |
| Linux: no install | `Ordnance-0.4.4-linux-x86_64.AppImage` |
| Linux: just the binary (needs WebKitGTK 4.1) | `Ordnance-0.4.4-linux-x64.tar.gz` |

**Browser extension:** `ordnance-extension-chrome-1.0.4.zip` or `ordnance-extension-firefox-1.0.4.zip`. Load it unpacked. On a Nexus Files tab, the button beside Manual download says Ordnance.
